package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5, 2020.2 with no hotfix, 2020.2 HF 1, 2020.2 HF 2 (as per public advisories)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion platform was compromised to include a highly sophisticated backdoor (SUNBURST) that enabled remote attackers to execute arbitrary code, exfiltrate sensitive data, and maintain persistent, covert access to victim environments. The malicious code was stealthily inserted into legitimate software updates, resulting in a widespread supply chain attack that impacted thousands of organizations globally, including government and critical infrastructure.

execution_context.trigger: at runtime, after the Orion service starts and initialization completes

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the Orion service starts, the code checks for security tools and analysis environments, waits a randomized interval to evade detection, then initiates outbound HTTP/S communication to a hardcoded C2 domain, receives attacker instructions or payloads, and executes them, enabling remote code execution and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes a covert, persistent communication channel to an external command-and-control (C2) server using obfuscated logic, incorporates anti-analysis and sandbox evasion techniques, and enables remote execution of attacker-supplied code—behaviors that are characteristic of advanced persistent threat (APT) malware and are never present in legitimate Orion DLLs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate SolarWinds Orion DLLs should not contain any logic for external C2 communication, anti-analysis or sandbox evasion, randomized execution delays, or the ability to execute arbitrary code received from the network.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate software may perform update checks or telemetry reporting, but these are implemented with transparent, documented endpoints and without obfuscation, anti-analysis logic, or the ability to execute arbitrary code from remote sources.
key_indicators: Obfuscated outbound HTTP/S requests to rare or newly registered domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Anti-analysis and sandbox evasion logic (e.g., environment checks for security tools, virtual machines, or debuggers)
Randomized execution delays before network activity
Dynamic loading and execution of code received from C2 server

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is surreptitiously inserted into the SolarWinds Orion update DLL (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) during the build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of the backdoor to customer environments via legitimate software updates.

attack_chain.action: Upon service start, the backdoor code checks for the presence of security tools, analysis environments, and virtual machines, and delays execution using a randomized timer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stealthy activation of the backdoor, evading automated analysis and detection.

attack_chain.action: The backdoor initiates outbound HTTP/S communication to a hardcoded C2 domain (e.g., avsvmcloud.com) using obfuscated logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of a covert channel for remote attacker control and payload delivery.

attack_chain.action: If instructed by the C2 server, the backdoor dynamically loads and executes attacker-supplied code or exfiltrates sensitive data from the victim environment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the victim environment, including data breach and persistent attacker access.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/S connections from Orion service processes to rare, newly registered, or known SUNBURST C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Presence of obfuscated or suspicious logic within SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll
Randomized delays (hours to days) before network activity initiated by Orion services
Anti-analysis or sandbox evasion checks (e.g., process, environment, or VM detection) within application DLLs
Dynamic code loading or execution within Orion service processes
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (with malicious modifications, hash mismatch from known-good versions)
Unexpected changes in Orion DLL file hashes compared to vendor-provided baselines
network_indicators: Additional secondary C2 domains as published in SolarWinds/SUNBURST IOCs (e.g., digitalcollege.org, incomeupdate.com, databasegalore.com)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion service processes for unexpected outbound HTTP/S connections to known SUNBURST C2 domains or rare, newly registered domains. Perform file integrity monitoring on SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll and related Orion DLLs to detect unauthorized modifications or hash mismatches. Use endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to identify anti-analysis logic, randomized execution delays, and dynamic code loading within Orion processes. Cross-reference observed network and file indicators with published IOCs from SolarWinds advisories and threat intelligence feeds.
